newsitem.title: CHINA: China says commissions hamper insurance growth.
newsitem.headline: China says commissions hamper insurance growth.

text.p: Excessive commissions awarded to China's insurance agents are the most urgent problem hampering the development of the fledgling insurance industry, the Business Weekly said on Sunday.
Although Chinese law limits commissions to five percent of premium income, many insurers were paying their agents up to 40 percent of premiums to compete for business, the newspaper said.

"Due to the limited quantity and important role of the insurance agents, insurance companies have vied with each other by adopting unstandardised measures," the newspaper quoted Pu Ying, secretary general of the Insurance Association of Beijing, as saying.
Local insurance firms across China were scrambling to increase market share after the launch last month of three large national insurers, the newspaper said.
Many agents had illegally raised premiums or commission rates or worked for several competing insurers at the same time, it said. Such actions had caused chaos in the market, it said.
China had long controlled its insurance market, once a monopoly of the state-run People's Insurance Company, but it has been gradually opening up the sector to both domestic and foreign competition.
That has led to the increase in commissions, according to industry officials.
The newspaper said that total premium income throughout the industry reached 60.1 billion yuan ($7.2 billion) last year.

American International Assurance Co Ltd, part of the American International Group and Tokio Marine & Fire Insurance Co Ltd have been allowed to issue policies in China while the Hong Kong unit of Manufacturers Life Insurance Co of Canada and Winterthur Insurance Co of Switzerland have been cleared for joint ventures.
Many other insurers have representative offices in China though these are barred from issuing policies.
Pu said that many representative offices of foreign insurers had secretly conducted direct insurance and agency business.
"As liaison organs, representative offices can only provide information for their headquarters and are not permitted to conduct operational business," Pu was quoted as saying.
He did not say whether any action was being considered to halt these practices. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
